decisions.reason: It fits the firm's core second-channel authentication proposition and should be inexpensive to keep available while market adoption and integration opportunities continue to unfold.
Mobile PDF signing is close to the firm's strategic direction in secure digital contracting, so the firm would likely keep this option open despite still-uncertain demand.
A multi-layer end-to-end security architecture is highly complementary to the firm's core capabilities and platform logic, making abandonment unlikely after only one year.
This looks like a narrower application-layer add-on with less certain standalone value, but as a software-based option it is still cheap enough to keep on the market for now.
A QR-code-based hardware signature token appears less aligned with the firm's move toward app-based cross-channel identity and is costlier to maintain as an option because of its hardware component.
Security compliance for payment-related networks matches the firm's regulated-security positioning, so management would likely retain it while learning more about customer traction.
